title: Lagged Bitcoin realized-cap 28-day growth long-or-cash policy
thesis: Positive four-week growth in Bitcoin realized capitalization may identify sustained capital absorption and a rising aggregate holder cost basis, supporting better subsequent BTC returns and drawdown paths than nonpositive-growth weeks.
mechanism: When coins move at progressively higher aggregate cost bases, the realized value of the network rises. A weekly, conservatively lagged signal may distinguish durable capital absorption from periods of cost-basis contraction, while an adversarial prior recognizes that the measure embeds BTC prices and can merely lag an existing bull market.
economic_rationale: A full-capital long-or-cash policy is useful only if positive-growth weeks preserve sufficient BTC upside while nonpositive weeks avoid drawdown enough to beat passive BTC after normal and doubled fee plus adverse-slippage costs, with annual breadth and no single episode or terminal inventory mark dominating the result.
